activeMission: NIGHTFALL: reconcile the open PR frontier, put durable zero-external-IO mesh liveness on a cron boundary, and establish what deployment actually exists.
completed: All five open PRs reconciled and closed: #177 merged with three repairs, #174 closed as a strict subset of it, #167 merged (reachability prose bound to the live graph), #168 and #178 merged as documentation.

Main was RED before this mission on tests/reachability-ratchet: twelve modules added in the prior thirty commits had no entry point and no classification. All twelve classified against honest gates; one new gate NO_PROVIDER_ADAPTER_CONFIGURED registered.

Eighteen modules carried a private copy of the canonical effect ledger. The existing single-definition guard matched only the canonical NAME, so seventeen aliased copies had walked past it. Guard now matches the key set; all eighteen import from effect-ledgers.mjs.

Cron boundary hardened: a schedule finer than the day-granularity occurrence key is refused rather than silently folding 288 firings into one; vercel.json and VERCEL_AGENT_MESH_CRON_SCHEDULE are bound by a test so drift cannot silently 403 every real invocation.

Zero-external-IO canary verified against REAL PostgreSQL through the real handler: first firing 200 with a durable cycle receipt; replay from a SEPARATE PROCESS returned duplicateDelivery true with the SAME cycleId; a conflicting source commit returned 409 scheduler-occurrence-identity-conflict; unauthorized paths 401/403/405 wrote nothing.
Reachability prose in CURRENT_SYSTEM_STATE reconciled to the live graph: 170 src modules, 109 production-reachable, 4 operator-only, 57 unreachable.
blockers: NO VERCEL PROJECT EXISTS. The account (team_A9LnjIuS5PU0rNetsHMu1N0r, Hobby) has zero projects. vercel.json declares a cron; nothing hosts it. Every deployment and production-health check is therefore n/a, not failing.

The project was deliberately NOT created: without DATABASE_URL and CRON_SECRET the route returns 503 on every firing, so a project deployed now would present a production surface whose daily cron always fails -- worse than none, because it looks deployed. A generated CRON_SECRET would also have to be handed over in chat, which is the wrong place for a credential.

GitHub Actions remains account/runner-infrastructure blocked; hosted zero-step runs are neither source failures nor source passes. All gate evidence in this handoff is local execution against real PostgreSQL.
